name: germany-law
label: Germany
record_note: Grundgesetz from 1949 (DocPatch reconciled with the official text, then Gesetze im Internet); all other federal law from 10 June 2019 (Gesetze im Internet via QuantLaw's daily archive). Checked against Gesetze im Internet on the record_to day.

dates.before_1970: git cannot store dates before 1970: those commits are dated 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, one second apart in order; the real date is in the In-Kraft trailer and the in-kraft/YYYY-MM-DD tag
dates.federal_in_force: for federal acts other than the Grundgesetz, the day Gesetze im Internet published the change; In-Kraft-laut-Fussnote gives the date the footnotes state where it differs

modifies.note: no record yet of law that changes in effect while its words stay the same

kinds.changed: the text of an act changed
kinds.added: an act first published (Neu aufgenommen, or under its amending law)
kinds.removed: an act no longer published for 14 days (Nicht mehr veröffentlicht)

changes.note: One commit per amending law per in-force day, across every act it changed; the author is the law.

scope.when_absent: no scope note is recorded in this history (no Applies lines yet); not a statement that a change reaches every case

default_reach.meaning: a law may not attach new burdens to facts already completed before its promulgation (true retroactivity, echte Rückwirkung), save narrow exceptions; it may in principle reach facts that began earlier and are still ongoing (false retroactivity, unechte Rückwirkung), subject to proportionality and legitimate expectations; criminal law is never retroactive (Art. 103(2) GG)
default_reach.authority: Rechtsstaatsprinzip, Art. 20(3) GG, as applied by the Bundesverfassungsgericht (e.g. BVerfGE 135, 1); Art. 103(2) GG

tool: python tools/stand_am.py DATE [ARTICLE ...] | python tools/stand_am.py DATE --gesetz <act>
